561ae0003c753e6c.justification: Abnormal motor-endplate transmission is broader than the specific molecular processes and effects listed.

3881aebb694a0190.justification: CMS refers to the general syndrome group without attribution to a candidate gene.

e1d9d2c61126704e.mention: molecular defects in the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor
e1d9d2c61126704e.justification: Acetylcholine receptor defects do not specify loss of function or any other listed molecular effect.

9b9f7dfa49df4cec.mention: defects in endplate development and maintenance

39216214cfde752c.justification: Defective glycosylation is not equivalent to protein misfolding or another listed mechanism.

a62f92b1885f0495.justification: Cholinergic agonists are a broader class and cannot be equated specifically with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

c9fbe91fd855b88a.mention: long-lived open-channel blockers of the acetylcholine receptor ion channel
c9fbe91fd855b88a.justification: No candidate represents acetylcholine receptor open-channel blockers; aminopyridines block potassium channels.

cac6db6ef86cb1bd.justification: None of the candidate therapies represents adrenergic agonists.

request_payload.title: Congenital myasthenic syndromes: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment.

mentions.sentence: The congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS) are a diverse group of genetic disorders caused by abnormal signal transmission at the motor endplate, a special synaptic contact between motor axons and each skeletal muscle fibre.

candidates.summary: Changes in SNAP25 cause early-onset epilepsy with developmental delay; one reported variant instead causes a presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome with fat

mentions.sentence: Present therapies for the CMS include cholinergic agonists, long-lived open-channel blockers of the acetylcholine receptor ion channel, and adrenergic agonists.

candidates.label: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (e.g. pyridostigmine)
candidates.summary: Drugs that make each released packet of acetylcholine act for longer at the neuromuscular junction. Reported to improve strength in SYT2-related presynaptic con

candidates.label: 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine)
candidates.summary: A potassium-channel blocker that lengthens the nerve signal so more neurotransmitter is released. Used in presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndromes; reported

candidates.label: Aminopyridines (4-AP / 3,4-DAP) as a presynaptic boost
candidates.summary: The same class of potassium-channel blockers, used to push more neurotransmitter release when a SNARE-machinery variant has weakened it. Reported for VAMP2 and

candidates.label: Structure-based pharmacological chaperones for Munc18-1
candidates.summary: Small molecules designed from the Munc18-1 structure to bind and stabilize the protein. Intended to replace generic chemical chaperones, which need high doses.

candidates.label: 4-Phenylbutyrate / glycerol phenylbutyrate (chemical chaperone)
candidates.summary: An FDA-approved drug (for urea-cycle disorders) that acts as a chemical chaperone, helping unstable or misfolded proteins fold and reach their working location.

candidates.label: scAAV9.P546.SLC6A1 intrathecal gene replacement
candidates.summary: A virus-delivered extra copy of SLC6A1, given into the spinal fluid, to restore GABA re-uptake. First-in-human trial is open by invitation.
